items.title: Inside the DNA and fingerprint effort to identify Rasuwa flood victims
items.summary: More than 6,000 people remain missing following the devastating flood on the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa. Most of the bodies recovered so far cannot be identified. According to the latest figures, 1,403 bodies have been found. Of these, only 103 have been identified and handed over to relatives. items.title: 24 days after flood, hunger grips three Rusuwa wards
items.summary: Food is running out in villages cut off after the Bhotekoshi flood swept away bridges.

items.title: Six bodies recovered from Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
items.summary: Rescue teams find the bodies of people missing since the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods as search continues inside the tunnel for possible further victims.

items.title: Wagle seeks India’s support for post-flood reconstruction
items.summary: In his first foreign visit as finance minister, Wagle asks Sitharaman for help in rebuilding infrastructure destroyed by the Bhotekoshi floods and discusses trade, investment and connectivity.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods disrupt schooling for 14,500 children in three districts
items.summary: More than 9,400 students have been directly affected, while schools being used as shelters are delaying the return to classes for thousands more.

items.title: Bridges gone, roads damaged, villages cut off from relief
items.summary: Helicopters and temporary crossings are helping deliver food and other essentials to cut-off communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, but officials say restoring roads and bridges must be an immediate priority.
